title: Felix and the Deadline
premise: Odile Lockridge, a sleepless interpreter embedded in a doomed peace delegation, is approached by Felix, a stranger who claims she once saved his life—a favor she has no memory of. He offers to erase her from the network that trained her as an asset, but the price is her testimony against it before the summit convenes. As Odile digs into the gaps in her own past, she discovers the 'incident' that broke her sleep was her own handler's assassination, and that the delegation's failure is being engineered by the very people who made her. In the end, Odile chooses truth over belonging: she interprets not the summit's speeches but the network's crimes into the open record, burning her trainers and finally sleeping through the night.
about_author: Kestrel Thackeray is a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working behind glass booths in Geneva, Vienna, and places without names on the itinerary. They write thrillers about people whose professional invisibility becomes their greatest liability.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Three weeks before the summit, Odile works the delegation's pre-negotiations on four hours of broken sleep. A man named Felix corners her after a session, thanking her for saving his life in Marseilles—an event she cannot recall—and leaves a card bearing no name, only a time and place. The beat is unease: kindness arriving like a debt collector.

chapters.title: Four Hours of Sleep
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile investigates her own memory, finding her Marseilles assignment logs redacted in her own handwriting. Her handler, Voss, reassures her with language that feels rehearsed. She nearly burns Felix's card but keeps it. Emotional beat: the horror of distrusting your own record.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix meets Odile at a shuttered tram depot and lays out the offer: he can extract her from the training program's registry before the summit, but first she must testify to what the network did—what they both are. He reveals he was trained alongside her; the favor is real, just buried. Beat: vertigo of a shared past she never knew.

chapters.title: Simultaneous
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. During a live delegation session, Odile realizes she is rendering one delegate's words with subtle distortions she didn't consciously choose—conditioned phrasing surfacing under stress. Voss watches her too closely from the gallery. Beat: the body betraying its training; loyalty to the delegation cracking against loyalty to herself.

chapters.title: The Incident, Replayed
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix walks Odile through recovered footage of Marseilles: she shielded him during a botched extraction, then watched Voss execute the team's courier—the incident her mind refuses to let her sleep through. The network ordered it; she was the witness they left alive on purpose. Beat: grief converting into purpose.

chapters.title: Dead Language
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile tests Voss with a deliberately mistranslated phrase known only to program graduates; his response confirms he's still active in the network and engineering the summit's collapse. She reports nothing, playing loyal while drafting her testimony with Felix. Beat: the intoxicating and terrifying freedom of double agency.

chapters.title: Extraction Protocol
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The network moves early—Felix's safehouse is burned and his contact inside the summit security detail turns up dead. He and Odile realize the registry purge must happen during the summit itself, when every asset will be in one building. Beat: the plan hardening from escape into attack.

chapters.title: Booth Nine
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Summit day. Odile takes her booth while Felix infiltrates the archive floor beneath the plenary hall. Voss feeds her a speech containing a trigger phrase meant to activate her as the network's instrument of sabotage. She recognizes it mid-sentence. Beat: white-knuckle control—interpreting betrayal in real time.

chapters.title: Rendering It Into the Record
chapters.summary: Odile's POV (climax). Instead of obeying the phrase, Odile goes off-script: she abandons the official translation and narrates the network's operation, Voss's murder of the courier, and the sabotage plan directly into the delegates' earpieces while Felix triggers the registry purge below. Security converges; Voss is arrested mid-exit. Beat: truth spoken aloud at last, at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Sleeping Through the Night
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Weeks later, the delegation limps toward an honest, smaller agreement, and Odile—no longer invisible, no longer theirs—testifies from a witness booth rather than an interpreter's. Felix, leaving for whatever comes next, tells her the debt is paid. She sleeps eight hours. Beat: quiet resolution; belonging chosen, not assigned.
